柏格醫生 dr berg 談：有些營養素，可自然去除血管的斑塊。
斑塊成分： 1.膽固醇 2.蛋白質 3.鈣 當動脈內發炎或有問題，這3成分會形成貼布（形成斑塊）。
斑塊有2種：軟斑塊(不穩定、危險)、硬斑塊(鈣化、穩定、危險性較低)。軟斑塊發生率，是鈣化斑塊4倍！
冠狀動脈鈣化測試(CAC)，可對動脈斑塊的數量進行評分。此測試主要檢測鈣化斑塊，因此分數通常不反映軟斑塊。
CAC矛盾是：改變飲食、清除壞東西，變健康後，CAC評分反而上升。這不代表斑塊惡化，而是軟斑塊已經穩定並變成硬斑塊。
軟斑塊與糖化和低密度脂蛋白(LDL)的更多氧化有關。
LDL有2種： 1.小的，稱緊密小顆粒LDL，更危險、更具致病性。 2.大的，稱漂浮大顆粒LDL，非致病性。
驗血數據中，可測出軟斑塊: 1. 髓過氧化酶Myeloperoxidase 2. 脂蛋白相關磷脂酶A2(Lp_PLA2)，均表示軟斑塊。 3. 頸動脈超音波(ultrasound)也可測出軟斑塊。
高密度脂蛋白(HDL)，很重要，HDL要上升，往往能清除致病性、壞LDL。另外，三酸甘油酯數值要低，數值高表示碳水吃太多。另外，脂蛋白胰島素阻抗測試也很重要，它與心血管動脈粥狀硬化的相關性，高於其他任何因素。
判斷緊密小顆粒與漂浮大顆粒LDL：驗 LDL÷ApoB(脂蛋白一部分，顯示顆粒數量)，大於1.2最好，顯示出LDL是漂浮大顆粒，非致病性。
去除動脈斑塊堆積的5營養： 1.碧蘿芷(Pycnogenol)吃150毫克 2.積雪草(Gotu Kola)吃450毫克 3.維生素K2高劑量的，是最有效血管鈣化抑制劑，建議吃Life Extention公司的Mega K2。 4.納豆激酶(Nattokinase) 5. 維生素B3(菸鹼酸,Niacin)，建議吃引起潮紅的B3.
清理血管斑塊，也有效的其他營養： 1.生育三烯酚(Tocotrienols) 2. 黃連素（小蘗鹼,berberine) 3.陳蒜(老的蒜頭) 4.鎂 5.鉀 6.維生素D3

歐米茄3有許多好處，包括保健心臟健康。 鮭魚和沙丁魚是最好的歐米茄3 來源之一，但是奇亞籽呢？ 如果以每克比較，奇亞籽是歐米茄3 的更高，但它們不是 DHA(活性歐米茄3)。 奇亞籽含有 ALA (轉化為活性歐米茄3前的形式)，只有 0.5% 會轉化為 DHA。
奇亞籽與蛋相比，一顆蛋含約 7 克蛋白質，而奇亞籽則含有 4 克。 蛋中的蛋白質是最容易吸收利用的蛋白質。
奇亞籽含有維生素E、維生素C、維生素B群、鈣、磷、鉀和鎂。
研究表明，奇亞籽的好處： 1. 保護心臟 2. 降血壓 3. 對大腦有益 4. 幫助稀釋血液
奇亞籽含可溶性纖維，是吃奇亞籽最顯著的好處。
製作健康的奇亞籽布丁： 1. 將 2 湯匙奇亞籽與半杯牛奶或不加糖杏仁奶混合。 2. 攪拌至種子膨脹並形成凝膠。 3. 加入克菲爾、莓果、希臘優格、椰子奶油或堅果。
奇亞籽與液體混合時形成的凝膠是微生物群的絕佳食物。 奇亞籽幫助緩解腸炎和便秘。它的凝集素含量也很低。
奇亞籽凝膠含有多酚 (polyphenols) －－是有益於微生物的植物化學物。 健康的微生物菌群保健您的情緒、能量和整體健康。 日常吃奇亞籽、發酵蔬菜、酸菜、泡菜和泡菜，以保持健康的微生物菌群。

作法： 1. 將牛奶倒入玻璃瓶罐，在頂部留出大約一英寸的空間。 2. 加入甜葉菊和奇亞籽，立即蓋上蓋子並搖勻。將其放在廚房檯上或冰箱中約10分鐘，然後再次搖動。然後放入冰箱幾個小時使其變稠。

ns2:group.ns2:title: Building Sovereignty: Where Your AI Runs Matters — XConf Europe 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Speaker: Jens Peveling
About the speaker: Jens is is an engineering leader and subject matter expert for souverign cloud platforms.His backgound is in of Software Architecture and Infrastructure Engineering. Currently, he is working in the energy sector, building Europes largest private and sovereign cloud platform from scratch.
About the talk: European organizations and governments racing to leverage AI and large-scale data analytics face an uncomfortable truth: the platforms they run their critical services on, train AI models on, the pipelines they feed sensitive data into, and the infrastructure governing their data residency are controlled by hyperscalers — architecturally unfit for true sovereignty. This talk is based on first-hand experience building a sovereign cloud from bare metal for the European energy sector. I present core concepts for building a platform designed for running critical workloads and data-intensive operations under full jurisdictional control — no hyperscaler dependencies, no shared-responsibility illusions. I examine why sovereign infrastructure is becoming a strategic necessity, not a niche concern: how data gravity, AI model training locality, and regulatory frameworks force a rethinking of where and how we build cloud platforms. The talk covers real trade-offs, real architecture decisions, and lessons learned the hard way.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Scaling ETL Migrations to 300x with AI — XConf Europe 2026

Speakers: Carolina Allende & Aakash Jain
About the speakers: Carolina is a machine learning engineer specializing in the bridge between complex research and scalable AI implementation. From developing hybrid classical-quantum models to architecting LLM and computer vision-powered solutions, she focuses on making AI practical, sustainable, and high-impact. She is deeply committed to helping bridge the gap that women in STEM face.
Aakash is a Lead data engineer with deep expertise in architecting and deploying scalable, cost-efficient data platforms. He specialises in transforming complex data challenges — from modernising legacy systems to building next-generation architectures across multi-cloud environments — and has extensive experience designing, building and optimising platforms that power GenAI solutions.
About the talk: Enterprises have been running critical data pipelines on aging platforms for decades and migrating them to GCP is genuinely hard.In this talk, we will share what actually happened when we combined engineering expertise with AI-assisted code translation on a large-scale migration. We built a human-in-the-loop workflow — not because it sounded good, but because full automation kept breaking things that mattered. The result: The first iteration we achieved 60x faster migration the goal was to ran 200–300× faster. The tradeoffs were real too. We’ll cover: ∙ What made the legacy platform so difficult to migrate ∙ How we designed the AI-assisted workflow and where we drew the human line ∙ What failed, what we fixed, and what we’d do differently ∙ What teams planning similar work should watch out for No vendor pitch. No cherry-picked metrics. Just delivery experience.

About the speaker: Prachi is a Lead Consultant at Thoughtworks, with around 17 years of experience in software engineering. She has worked across distributed systems and complex legacy modernization, with a strong focus on architecture, continuous delivery, and scalable software design.More recently, she has been exploring AI/ML and Generative AI, especially how they can support developer workflows and help teams work with complex systems more effectively.
About the talk: "egacy systems are easy to dismiss as old technology, but in many organizations they are still the systems the business depends on every day. They carry years of decisions, exceptions, workarounds, integrations, and operational history. The difficult part is that this complexity is rarely visible in one place, which makes even small changes feel slower and riskier than they should.

ns2:group.ns2:description:
Speaker: Chris Ford, Technology Director at Thoughtworks
About the the talk: Coding agents make a big difference to how individual developers do their job. Some activities, in particular those relating to the production of code, can be a whole lot faster.
Coding agents also make a big difference to how we run engineering organisations, because they have traditionally been shaped by the constraint that code was very expensive to produce. Examples of how organisation-level processes change include how we treat legacy code, how we design architecture and how we decide whether to buy something off-the-shelf or build it ourselves.
The changing economics of software will reshape the context within which every software developer works. If you understand these dynamics, you have a better chance to take advantage of the opportunities.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Jam-oriented programming: Bringing improvisational jazz to engineering — XConf Europe 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Jam-oriented programming: Bringing improvisational jazz to engineering — XConf Europe 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Speaker: Lu Wilson
About the speaker: Lu creates surreal films about their creative coding projects under the Todepond moniker. They're an active part of the global live coding and algorave community, as well as the mass collaborative leaderless group known as "Pastagang" where they contribute to open source music-making software. In their day job, Lu designs and builds experimental prototypes as a contractor, and is currently working with the Wikimedia Foundation.
About the talk: Jam-oriented programming' is the joke name of a new style of software development that is no joke at all. It adopts the practices and mentalities of an informal jam session to an extreme extent.
In a typical jam, there is no one in charge and anyone can make any sound they want at any time they choose. In jam-oriented programming, it's the same. Anyone can add, edit or delete code without any permission. Everyone is admin, nothing is certain and anything can happen. It sounds like chaos and it is. But it's also surprisingly successful, with entire music-making tools appearing overnight out of the multi-headed process and even a published academic paper to accompany it all.
How and why is this even possible? And what does it tell us about the way we collaborate as developers?

ns2:group.ns2:title: The Augmented Engineer: Evolving Sensible Defaults through Human-Centric AI — XConf Europe 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Speaker: Elena Guidi, Senior Consultant, Tech Lead, Thoughtworks
About the talk: Engineering excellence at Thoughtworks has always been defined by our Sensible Defaults,the collective wisdom that reduces decision fatigue and keeps us focused on value. Today, AI is redefining that baseline. While we are still actively defining what this new baseline looks like, the true shift isn't in the automation itself, but in why human practitioners remain more critical than ever.
In this session, I explore the personal experience of the ""augmented engineer."" We’ll move beyond the hype of agents to discuss AI as a disciplined tool for our daily craft. Drawing from real-world workflows, I will share how to integrate AI into your personal ""defaults"" with concrete examples, such as using it to scaffold refactoring, or bridge niche tech stack gaps without sacrificing technical integrity. This is about elevating our human potential, ensuring that while the tools change, the curiosity, judgment, and responsibility remain firmly in our hands.

ns2:group.ns2:title: What Agents Do When You’re Not Looking — XConf Europe 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Speaker: Matias Vizcaino
About the speaker: Matias is a Lead Data Engineer specialising in data platforms, governance, and engineering practices that help teams deliver safely at scale. He works across data platform architecture, data product delivery, automation, and privacy-aware systems, and is increasingly focused on the practical realities of AI-first delivery: how teams can use autonomous coding agents confidently, without losing sight of quality, observability, and control.
About the talk: Coding agents have evolved fast: from chat assistants, to copilots, to increasingly autonomous systems that can plan, delegate and act. That shift is exciting, but it also creates a new engineering problem: what are these systems actually doing when we are not watching closely? In this talk, I’ll trace that evolution, starting with war stories from the industry that make the risks feel real and familiar. Then I’ll share what I’ve learned from building and observing my own agent teams in Claude: the funny moments, the unexpected interactions, and the patterns that only become visible when you look at traces and behaviour instead of demos. I’ll close with the emerging practitioner playbook for this space: how teams are starting to observe, evaluate and govern agents so we can use them with more confidence in real-world delivery.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]AI-First Software Maintenance & AI-First Software Delivery — XConf Europe 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: AI-First Software Maintenance & AI-First Software Delivery — XConf Europe 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Speakers: Vitória Regina Ragazzon Toebe Amy Pellegrini
About the speakers: Vitória Toebe is a Tech Lead and developer at Thoughtworks, focused on software maintenance, operations, and AI-first practices beyond delivery. She is curious and people oriented by nature. Her work focuses on support maintenance and management powered with AI, helping teams resolve issues faster, collaborate through complexity, and continuously improve production systems.
Amy is a Tech Lead and software consultant at Thoughtworks, helping clients navigate complex delivery and stakeholder dynamics. Amy is particularly interested in the intersection of product development and AI-first software delivery, and the human challenges that it brings. Their main focus is finding the balance between well established software development practices and cutting edge AI technologies.
About the talk: Most conversations about AI in software engineering focus on shipping features faster. But in a fast-moving environment, the real bottleneck often lives on the other side: the time between a reported issue and a confident resolution. We'll share how a maintenance team and a delivery team — working on a core service with multiple consumers, spread across internal and external teams, investigating issues across multiple data sources — operate as one connected AI-first system. With workflows designed around AI strengths: triage, data correlation, supporting cross-team communication, and handling context cleanly between maintenance and delivery.
You'll leave with concrete patterns for AI-first incident management, a model for maintenance-delivery collaboration that scales, and an honest view of where AI helps — and where it still gets in the way.

ns2:group.ns2:title: 中國Z世代為何迷上玄學拜佛？ 什麼是「心靈經濟」？－ BBC News 中文
ns2:group.ns2:description:
中國年輕人湧向寺廟、算命、塔羅牌和各類靈修產品。這未必是因為他們找到了宗教信仰，而是因為在充滿不確定性的時代，他們正試圖尋求一絲寄託。
面對就業、收入與未來的焦慮，許多人希望藉此尋求運氣、心安以及掌控感。對某些人來說，這意味著去寺廟上香祈福或算命求籤；對另一些人來說，則是購買號稱能帶來好運的手鍊、符咒等各類產品。
商界也敏銳地捕捉到了這一趨勢。無論是品牌還是寺廟，都正積極搶灘這個日益蓬勃的「心靈經濟」（spiritual economy），將古老傳統與現代神秘學轉化為針對新一代消費者的商品與體驗。
本集Asia Specific節目將一同剖析：這究竟是精神信仰的真正復興，抑或只是年輕人在面對日益迷茫的未來時，另一種求個心安、分散風險的方式？

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [格斗大视野]一拳KO直接轉身離開！馬克亨特從K-1打到UFC，為何被稱為MMA最硬無冕之王？

ns2:group.ns2:title: 一拳KO直接轉身離開！馬克亨特從K-1打到UFC，為何被稱為MMA最硬無冕之王？
ns2:group.ns2:description:
有些拳手KO對手之後，會衝上去補拳、怒吼、慶祝，生怕全場不知道自己贏了。但馬克・亨特不一樣。
他一拳打中，轉身就走。不是裝酷，也不是不尊重對手，而是因為他太清楚自己的拳頭有多重。拳頭落下的那一刻，答案已經寫完了。
他不是UFC冠軍，卻是無數拳迷心中分量最重的無冕之王。他個子不高，身材敦實，看起來不像傳統意義上的完美格鬥家，卻靠一雙鐵拳和一副鐵下巴，從街頭一路打進K-1世界大賽，又從PRIDE打到UFC，留下了無數讓拳迷熱血沸騰的名場面。
年輕時的馬克・亨特，只是新西蘭街頭一個愛打架的狠角色。直到一次夜店衝突，他幾分鐘內放倒多人，被拳館老闆看中，才第一次明白：原來同樣是打架，在街頭會進局子，在擂台上卻能換獎金。
從六包啤酒的野拳賽獎品，到K-1世界大賽冠軍，馬克・亨特靠的不是漂亮技術，也不是華麗包裝，而是最原始的硬度。你打我，我不倒；我打你，你必須躺下。
在K-1，他硬剛法國生化人勒・班納，拖著世界級踢拳殺手進入自己的泥潭，最終站上東京巨蛋的最高點。
在PRIDE，他面對「戰警」米爾科・克羅科普，被那記招牌高掃踢倒後，居然還能晃晃悠悠站起來。幾年後二番戰，他又用自己的臉、下巴和拳頭告訴戰警：你的左腿確實恐怖，但沒法把我送進墳墓。
到了UFC，很多人以為這個K-1老炮已經過氣。可馬克・亨特面對兩米一三的斯特魯夫，一記重拳打裂對手下巴，隨後頭也不回地轉身離開，留下了UFC重量級最經典的walk-off KO之一。
但馬克・亨特後半段的UFC生涯，讓人記住的不只是KO，還有他的怒火。
他和「大腳」席爾瓦打滿五回合，血戰成為UFC重量級經典，結果賽後對手藥檢不合格。後來面對布洛克・萊斯納，又一次遇到藥檢風波。對馬克・亨特來說，這不是簡單的輸贏，而是對格鬥純粹性的羞辱。
所以他開罵，開告，直接和UFC硬剛到底。
有人說他太軸，不懂變通。可這恰恰是馬克・亨特最珍貴的地方。他從街頭打到擂台，從來不是一個圓滑的人。他只認一個死理：靠拳頭吃飯，就得打得乾淨。
本期《格鬥大視野》，帶你重新看懂馬克・亨特：這個看起來像燒烤攤大叔的胖子，為什麼能從K-1打到PRIDE，再打進UFC，成為MMA史上最有味道、最硬骨頭的無冕之王。
你最喜歡馬克・亨特哪一個名場面？是一拳打裂斯特魯夫下巴後轉身離開，還是硬剛戰警克羅科普的復仇之戰？歡迎在評論區留下你的看法。 #mma #ufc #格斗

電解質是帶電荷的化學物質，是礦物質的鈉和鉀。
該唧筒的主要目的是保持鈉從細胞中流出,鉀保留在細胞內部.
